C0.quote: We study diversity in approval-based committee elections with incomplete or inaccurate information.
C0.note: Approval-based committee voting; computational query complexity.

C1.note: Query complexity bounds and approximation algorithms (AL) dominate. Approximation of Max Cover optimum coded WD. Experiments on Polis data (EM) and synthetic data (SI).

C2.1.quote: The sequence of sets A = (A(1), . . . , A(n)) is called the approval profile

C2.2.quote: every voter vi ∈ V approves of a subset of the candidates.

C2.3.quote: voters can become inaccurate in representing their true beliefs
C2.3.note: True approvals/beliefs referenced as held attitude.

C2.4.quote: the voters are inaccurate in reporting their true approvals
C2.4.note: Inaccurate setting separates reported from true approvals (A_p vs A).

C3.1.quote: we assume each query A(i, j) is incorrect with a probability p.
C3.1.note: Misreports are random noise, not strategic; no analysis has voters strategically submitting differing inputs.

C3.2.note: In incomplete/accurate setting, answers are taken as the true approval profile implicitly (A(i,j) defined directly); no statement of sincerity in words. Checked model, intro, conclusion.

C4.1.note: No voter utility, welfare or satisfaction notion used besides coverage score; Chamberlin-Courant score counts represented voters, not utility.

C5.1.quote: the Chamberlin-Courant (CC) score of a committee W
C5.1.note: Evaluates committees by number of voters with a representative (representation/diversity); results are on this.

C5.2.note: Score is computed on approval profile; in the inaccurate setting the goal is the score w.r.t. true approvals A, which is held-like, but the no-noise case evaluates the input without relating to held attitudes. Closest: INPUT-UNSTATED.

VOT.quote_behav: Samples of X are independent between voters, between candidates
VOT.note: Voters answer queries, randomly corrupted with probability p; fixed by model, not strategic.

ORG.note: The querying algorithm is a computational procedure, not an agent choosing in a game-theoretic model.

claims.quote: diverse summarizations can guarantee higher inclusivity
we prove diverse committees can be found by querying only a small fraction
our algorithms perform well also on smaller instances

C9.1.note: Claims about deliberation platforms and real instances; weak claims about institutions.

C9.2.quote: voters can become inaccurate in representing their true beliefs
C9.2.note: Claim that diverse committees summarize group opinion needs assumption that answered approvals equal true opinions in the accurate setting, and that missing/neutral votes are disapprovals (stated in Appendix E); the sincerity link is not stated.
